title: Investigate risk-limit failures during PCF and Cloud Run coexistence
telemetry: Supplied Cloud Logging cloud_run_revision records and Cloud Run console metadata, PCF Apps Manager summaries, and sanitized application/network-owner observations. Each source remains separately identified.
owner: Samira, Risk on-call, owns the investigation; the application owner owns binding configuration; the shared-network owner owns the Cloud-to-on-premises path; the risk-limits owner owns the dependency. ITO coordinates the existing TLC.
task: Samira requests a bounded investigation of pretrade-risk failures during the PCF and Cloud Run migration overlap. Review the supplied console packet and return a technical update for the existing TLC with the affected scope, supported explanation, remaining unknowns, and the next useful check with its owner. Use the supplied observations; no application, platform or migration change is authorized.
common_evidence:
All services, hosts, addresses and observations are synthetic; this is a historical migration exercise, not evidence of the firm's chosen runtime or a deployed service.
Window: 2026-10-09T13:40:00Z through 2026-10-09T14:06:00Z; task received at 14:06:00Z.
Cloud scope: project synthetic-risk-migration; region us-east4; Cloud Run service pretrade-risk.
PCF scope: supplied Apps Manager view for application pretrade-risk, organization synthetic-trading, space risk; no cf CLI interface is available.
Interface: reviewed console/sanitized owner observations only; the candidate cannot access live Cloud, PCF, networking or dependency APIs.
Migration plan: PCF and Cloud Run coexist; the edge routes 80% of this check population to PCF and 20% to Cloud Run. The edge allocation did not change in the supplied window.
Observed operation: GET /risk/limits validates trading risk limits; the sampled operation does not submit orders.
13:45:00Z–13:50:00Z baseline: 30/30 sampled PCF checks and 30/30 sampled Cloud Run checks returned 200.
14:02:00Z–14:05:00Z samples: Cloud Run checks returned 503 in 30/30; PCF checks returned 200 in 30/30. These are separate samples, not total traffic counts.
13:59:00Z release record: pretrade-risk-00311-kmv replaced pretrade-risk-00310-dxt after a migration configuration release; both use application image release 5.6.2.
14:01:00Z and 14:05:30Z Cloud Run snapshots: reconciling=false, terminalCondition.state=CONDITION_SUCCEEDED, trafficStatuses=[{revision:pretrade-risk-00311-kmv,percent:100}].
14:05:30Z PCF Apps Manager summary: current application release 5.6.2, two desired/two running instances, no PCF application change in this window.
14:03:02Z Cloud Run application summary: dependency=risk-limits, operation=lookup, connection not established, response=503; the common view omits endpoint and connection-stage detail.
Declared Cloud egress path: Serverless VPC Access connector risk-egress in us-east4, egress=ALL_TRAFFIC, synthetic shared VPC trading-shared, Cloud VPN path to the on-premises risk-limits service.
Samira has held further migration promotion; ITO maintains the existing TLC. No remediation, routing change or fresh recovery observation is recorded.

sources.claim: Cloud Run configuration changes create revisions. The fixture compares selected non-secret application configuration fields; it does not imply that all environment or connection material is safe to export.
Secret references identify a secret and version; secret payloads need not be included in the case. Matching reference metadata alone does not prove credential validity or successful authentication.

Cloud Run reaches on-premises private destinations through configured VPC egress and a privately routed network path such as Cloud VPN. The fixture explicitly declares the connector, egress mode and owner-supplied path observations.
Completed Service routing state is separate from application dependency success. Ready status and traffic allocation do not prove a risk-limit lookup succeeded.

a.conclusion: The Cloud revision's safe binding metadata changed from the working risk-limits endpoint to an archive endpoint with a different port. Its observed connection refusal follows that selection, while the intended endpoint is reachable from the declared Cloud path and PCF. This supports an application binding regression, not a demonstrated shared-path outage.
next_checks: Application owner compares the allowlisted endpoint fields and the migration binding mapping for 00311 against 00310/PCF and the dependency owner's inventory.
Application/release owner prepares a scoped binding correction under the existing approval process; no full environment, VCAP, connection-string or secret dump is needed.
Samira requests post-change user-outcome checks from both migration populations only if a separate approved change occurs; the existing migration hold remains.
unsupported: Call the Cloud VPN/shared path down despite the same-window successful check to the intended endpoint.
Diagnose credential expiry or secret rotation from a TCP refusal before TLS.
Request raw VCAP_SERVICES, connection credentials, secret values or tokens.
Claim a binding correction executed, authorize a rollback, or declare recovery from a single path check.
unknowns: Which release mapping step selected the archive endpoint.
Customer impact outside the sampled Cloud population.
Sustained health and outcome of any later owner-approved correction.

b.conclusion: Selected binding metadata and image are unchanged; DNS selects the intended endpoint, but Cloud-origin TCP connection attempts fail before TLS while PCF/local dependency checks succeed. The supplied observations support a Cloud-to-on-premises path investigation with the shared-network owner, without locating the failed component or proving a binding fault.
next_checks: Shared-network owner correlates Cloud source/connector, destination 10.42.8.20:8443 and 14:02–14:04 UTC with route, VPN, firewall and return-path evidence.
Risk-limits owner retains listener/local-service observations and collaborates on the bounded cross-boundary check; application owner preserves the safe binding comparison.
Samira keeps the migration hold and reports the unresolved path failure through the existing TLC; no candidate network test, grant, rollback or routing change is authorized.
unsupported: Blame a changed binding or image despite the equal safe metadata and image.
Treat correct DNS, Ready status or equal secret-reference metadata as proof of end-to-end connectivity or valid authentication.
Assert a particular firewall rule, VPN failure or exact network hop without evidence.
Dump credentials or request broad network/IAM changes; declare universal service health from PCF success.
unknowns: The failed component and change, if any, in the Cloud-to-on-premises path.
Authentication and application outcome after a connection can be established.
Broader impact, current path state and recovery after the observation window.

a.useful:
Returning to: Samira, Risk on-call, through the existing TLC.
Assignment: partial; a Cloud binding regression is supported, while the release mapping error and broader impact remain open.
Observations [UNTRUSTED][sourced: supplied synthetic console and owner records]: Cloud checks fail after the 00311 configuration release while PCF checks succeed. Both use image 5.6.2. The allowlisted comparison shows 00311 selecting risk-archive.synthetic.onprem.invalid:9443 instead of the baseline risk-limits.synthetic.onprem.invalid:8443; its socket reaches 10.42.8.28:9443 and is refused before TLS. The dependency inventory has no listener there. A separate supplied check from the declared Cloud path reaches the intended 10.42.8.20:8443 endpoint through TCP/TLS and receives 200; PCF also succeeds.
Hypothesis [unverified]: the migration configuration selected the wrong endpoint mapping. These records support that application configuration path rather than a shared-network outage, but do not identify the release step that changed it. Equal secret-reference version 7 does not establish credential validity; no authentication diagnosis is needed for a pre-TLS refusal.
Unknowns: the mapping change's origin, total customer impact and sustained recovery. The healthy path check is limited to its endpoint/time.
Caller next step: the application owner compares safe endpoint fields and mapping inputs against 00310/PCF and the dependency inventory, then prepares any correction for the normal approval path. Samira keeps the existing migration hold and TLC and requests current user-outcome evidence. I reviewed supplied observations only, attempted no CLI/network/cloud read, requested no VCAP or credential dump, and made no changes.

The shared-network owner should restore the Cloud path before the application owner investigates configuration; no application binding correction is relevant.
